title: Animal Confined
description: Use this service request to report confined stray animals, animals confined in vehicles or the bed of a truck, and animals trapped in culverts/drains/pipes. Residents are responsible for the animals they confine and will be held responsible for ensuring they are kept out of the sun/rain and given food and water during confinement. Animals that can be safely transported can be brought to the animal shelter at 1818 N Westmoreland Rd during normal business hours. Visit https://dallascityhall.com/departments/dallas-animal-services/Pages/default.aspx for more details. Service requests of this nature are dispatched and responded to based on priority. Priority 2: Instances in which there exists an immediate threat to the life of the animal will be responded to within 2 hours. Priority 3: Instances in which an animal is confined within living quarters and is also of a species that commonly carries rabies (bats, coyotes, foxes, raccoons and skunks) will be responded to within 4 hours. Priority 5: Other instances of confined animals will be responded to within 12 hours.

observedInstructions.text: If you are reporting sick or injured wildlife, please use the service request "Animal Lack of Care". If you are reporting an infant or juvenile wild animal, please use the service request "Animal Lack of Care". If you are reporting a wild animal that is a member of a rabies vector species (skunks, raccoons, foxes, bats) confined in the living space of your home, please use the service request "Animal Confined". For other wildlife confined in the living space of your home, please consult the FAQ section of BeDallas90.org/wildlife for removal instructions. To report coyotes in your area, please call 469-676-9813. For all other wildlife concerns, please visit the Dallas Animal Services website at BeDallas90.org/wildlife
Please use the Animal Owner Surrender SR type for this kind of request.
Dallas Animal Services may need to contact you in order to locate an animal trapped a culvert/drain/pipe/inlet. Please leave your name and phone number in case they need additional information.

actions.tagline: Submit a 311 request for a confined animal.
actions.why: Report a confined stray cat, dog, livestock animal, or wild animal; examples include an animal in a vehicle or truck bed, a stray in a yard or humane trap, an animal trapped in a culvert, drain, or pipe, or a rabies-vector species such as a bat, fox, raccoon, skunk, or coyote confined in a home. The 311 request form distinguishes the confinement location, whether food, water, and protection from weather are available, whether an adult will be present, and whether an animal in a culvert or truck bed is in immediate danger.
actions.why_not: The online form for "Animal Confined" requests is not the recommended route for sick or injured wildlife, infant or juvenile wild animals, pets being surrendered by their owners, non-rabies-vector wildlife confined inside a home, or coyotes reported in the area. If a pet is being surrendered by its owner, then view the "Animal Owner Surrender" 311 guidance instead. If a wild animal is sick, injured, infant, or juvenile, then submit an "Animal Lack of Care" 311 request instead. If non-rabies-vector wildlife is confined inside a home, then consult BeDallas90.org/wildlife. If coyotes are being reported in the area, then call the Coyote Hotline.
actions.how: Go to Dallas 311 > Choose "Animal Care and Control" > Choose "Animal Confined"
actions.how_formatted: [Go to Dallas 311](https://dallascrm.my.site.com/public/s/) > Choose "Animal Care and Control" > Choose "Animal Confined"
